content.title: Thousands gather at Cocoa Beach Air Show to celebrate America’s 250th
content.text: COCOA BEACH, Fla. — Thousands of people are enjoying the Cocoa Beach Air Show, and for some, this year’s event means something more as the country celebrates the United States’ 250th birthday. What You Need To Know Thousands attended the Cocoa Beach Air Show, many with personal ties to the military Spectators say the event is both thrilling and deeply meaningful The F-16 Viper Demo Team dedicated performances to service members past and present Organizers say the show brings people together during a time of national reflection Kyle McAuley is one of the thousands who traveled to Cocoa Beach for the show. He and his family made the trip from Clermont to see the action. “My uncle, he was in the Blue Angels. He got us tickets, and I wanted to experience this,” McAuley said. “A lot of my family is in the service too, so I have a big background in that and it’s really honorable.” The show featured a variety of aircraft and performances, including the Blue Angels, the B-52 Stratofortress, parachuters, and the F-16 Viper Demo Team. “The F-16 Viper Demo Team we really love to showcase the raw mite of the F-16 to the American people. We love to dedicate our performance to the veterans, those currently serving and those looking to serve,” said Captain Paul Howell with the F-16 Viper Demo Team. Howell has been flying for five years and has served in the military for 16 years. He said participating in the show carries deep personal meaning. “This is all I ever wanted to do in life was serve my country somehow and to get this kind of support from home crowds means the world to me,” Howell said. As the nation celebrates America’s 250th birthday, organizers say events like the Cocoa Beach Air Show help unite communities. Chris Dirato, Director of Public Relations for the Cocoa Beach Air Show, said, “You’re watching people protect our freedom every day. We know there’s a lot going on in the world these days so it’s very nice to see what they do for us.” For those who missed the show, there is another opportunity to attend. The air show continues Sunday, April 11, with gates opening at 9 a.m. at Lori Wilson Park.
